def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    colors = {v for row in grid for v in row if v != 7}
    target = next(color for color in colors
                  if any(grid[r][c] == color and grid[r+1][c] == color and
                         grid[r][c+1] == color and grid[r+1][c+1] == color
                         for r in range(h-1) for c in range(w-1)))
    cells = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == target]
    top = min(r for r, c in cells)
    bottom = max(r for r, c in cells)
    left = min(c for r, c in cells)
    right = max(c for r, c in cells)
    size = max(bottom-top+1, right-left+1)
    r, c = bottom-size+1, left+size-1
    out = [[7]*w for _ in range(h)]
    for _ in range(size):
        out[r][c] = target
        r += 1
        c -= 1
    return out
```

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    objects = {}
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if grid[r][c] != 7:
                objects.setdefault(grid[r][c], []).append((r, c))
    # The source square is the object with the greatest bounding-box extent.
    color, cells = max(objects.items(), key=lambda item: max(
        max(r for r, c in item[1]) - min(r for r, c in item[1]) + 1,
        max(c for r, c in item[1]) - min(c for r, c in item[1]) + 1))
    top = min(r for r, c in cells)
    bottom = max(r for r, c in cells)
    left = min(c for r, c in cells)
    right = max(c for r, c in cells)
    size = max(bottom-top+1, right-left+1)
    # Use the diagonal on which the object has more marked cells.
    main = sum(1 for r, c in cells if r-top == c-left)
    anti = sum(1 for r, c in cells if r-top+c-left == size-1)
    out = [[7]*w for _ in range(h)]
    for i in range(size):
        r, c = (top+i, left+i) if main > anti else (top+i, right-i)
        if 0 <= r < h and 0 <= c < w:
            out[r][c] = color
    return out
```

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    objects = {}
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if grid[r][c] != 7:
                objects.setdefault(grid[r][c], []).append((r, c))
    # The square outline is the object having the largest bounding box.
    color, cells = max(objects.items(), key=lambda item: max(
        max(r for r, c in item[1]) - min(r for r, c in item[1]) + 1,
        max(c for r, c in item[1]) - min(c for r, c in item[1]) + 1))
    top = min(r for r, c in cells)
    bottom = max(r for r, c in cells)
    left = min(c for r, c in cells)
    right = max(c for r, c in cells)
    size = max(bottom-top+1, right-left+1)
    # A down-left diagonal is used unless the box reaches the left edge.
    out = [[7]*w for _ in range(h)]
    if left > 0:
        r, c = top+size-1, right
        for _ in range(size):
            out[r][c] = color
            r -= 1
            c -= 1
    else:
        r, c = top, right
        for _ in range(size):
            out[r][c] = color
            r += 1
            c -= 1
